content_sections.heading: About MACS-ARI
content_sections.text: MACS-Agharkar Research Institute (ARI), Pune is an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India. It describes itself as committed to promoting science and technology, with emphasis on high standards of research and development. Its research covers the biological sciences in six thematic areas: Biodiversity & Palaeobiology, Bioenergy, Bioprospecting, Developmental Biology, Genetics & Plant Breeding, and Nanobioscience.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: The notice advertises 2 Scientist-C posts on a direct recruitment basis. The place of work for the first post is the Genetics & Plant Breeding Group of ARI, Pune. For the second post, it is the Developmental Biology Group of ARI, Pune.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: ARI invites applications from eligible Indian citizens and from scientists and employees of Central or State Governments, universities, recognised research institutions, public sector undertakings and other government-funded organisations. Essential: First Class M.Sc in Agriculture with specialisation in Genetics and Plant Breeding or allied disciplines from a recognised university or Institute, or equivalent qualifications. Four years of research and development experience in the required areas, as evidenced by publications in journals of repute, after obtaining an academic degree. Desirable: Doctoral degree in Genetics & Plant Breeding/ Plant Breeding/ Crop Improvement or allied disciplines from a recognised University or Institute. Proven experience in crop breeding and genomics-assisted research. Hands-on experience with field experimentation, phenotyping and data analysis. A demonstrated record of high-impact scientific publications and of taking part in acquiring and carrying out research projects. Ability to work collaboratively in interdisciplinary research programs. Experience in a research laboratory after obtaining an M.Sc in the relevant field. Essential: First Class M.Sc in Life Sciences, Biochemistry, Biotechnology or related fields, or equivalent qualifications. Four years of research and development experience in the required areas, evidenced by publications in reputed journals, after obtaining an academic degree. Desirable: Ph.D in areas of life science including Molecular biology, cell biology, and developmental biology or related areas. At least 3-5 years of post-doctoral experience in cell and developmental biology, with experience in cell culture and model organism research, and a good publication record in reputed journals. Experience of working in a research laboratory after obtaining an M.Sc. Time spent acquiring the essential qualifications does not count towards experience. However, time spent on a Doctorate degree from a recognised University or Institution (up to a maximum of two years) counts as experience. So does time spent on Post Doctorate research in a University or research institute, up to a maximum of two years, when it is shown by a certificate from that University or Institute and by research published in journals of repute. All educational, professional and technical qualifications must be from a recognised Board or University. For both posts, the upper age limit for direct recruitment shall not exceed 40 years. The crucial date for deciding the age limit and eligibility is the closing date for submission of applications. For the discipline-specific eligibility of each post, check the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: Both Scientist-C posts are permanent and carry Level-11 in the pay matrix (Rs.67700-208700), plus allowances as admissible. The notice says the pay, allowances and other benefits include NPS, Medical reimbursement, LTC etc., which are presently admissible as per the rules of the Institute. Selected candidates will be governed by the NPS Rules. Scientists C serve a probation period of one year, which may be extended at the discretion of the Competent Authority. Selected candidates are liable to serve anywhere in India and abroad.

content_sections.heading: ARI Pune Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: Undertake a breeding programme in wheat, soybean and grape for high yield, improved quality and tolerance to biotic and abiotic stresses. Implement genomic-assisted breeding approaches, including GWAS, QTL mapping, SNP-based analyses and genomic selection (GS). Develop, manage and evaluate bi-parental, multi-parent (MAGIC/NAAM) and RIL breeding populations. Conduct biofortification research and trait discovery for nutritional and quality-related traits. Plan, conduct and analyse multi-location and multi-season field trials. Carry out germplasm characterisation, evaluation and core collection development. Apply marker-assisted selection (MAS) and integrate molecular tools into breeding pipelines. Perform plant phenotyping using morphological, physiological and biochemical methods. Conduct quality analyses, including oil, protein, minerals, fatty acid compositions and volatile profiling. Contribute to seed production programmes and varietal release pipelines as per institutional and national guidelines. Publish research outcomes in peer-reviewed journals with a high impact factor. Prepare and submit research project proposals and secure extramural funding from national and international agencies. Assist in mentoring research scholars and contribute to departmental and institutional academic and other activities. Initiate and develop independent projects in new and emerging frontiers of cell and developmental biology, organelle biology and diseases. Secure extramural funding. Enthuse, motivate and supervise research scholars. Take part in teaching and training programs, and in teaching and training students. Contribute towards the development and maintenance of Institutional infrastructure. Facilitate and carry out various academic outreach activities. Advance research in cell and developmental biology and start new transnational areas of research. Contribute to Institutional work as entrusted from time to time.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Having the essential qualifications does not by itself entitle a candidate to an interview. A committee decides whether a qualification is equivalent to the essential and desirable qualifications. If many applications are received, the Institute may limit the number of candidates called for interview through shortlisting. The shortlisting criteria may include desirable qualifications and/or experience beyond the minimum. Only shortlisted candidates will be informed by email of the date, time and venue of the next stage of selection. Outstation candidates called for interview will be paid two-tier AC rail fare both ways by the shortest route. A reserve panel, in order of merit, will be prepared from the candidates called for interview. It remains valid for one year from the date of interview and may be used to fill the advertised vacancy and vacancies arising later.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are there in ARI Pune Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are 2 vacancies, both unreserved (UR). One is for Scientist- 'C' in the Genetics & Plant Breeding Group and one is for Scientist- 'C' in Developmental Biology.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for ARI Pune Scientist-C posts?
faq.answer: The last date is 30 days from the date the advertisement is published in the Employment News. It is 45 days for candidates in the north-eastern states, Ladakh Division, Lahaul and Spiti, Pangi Sub Division, Andaman and Nicobar Island and Lakshadweep.

faq.question: Q3. What qualification is needed for the ARI Pune Scientist-C posts?
faq.answer: The Genetics & Plant Breeding post needs a First Class M.Sc in Agriculture with specialisation in Genetics and Plant Breeding or allied disciplines. The Developmental Biology post needs a First Class M.Sc in Life Sciences, Biochemistry, Biotechnology or related fields. Both posts also need four years of R&D experience, as evidenced by publications.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for ARI Pune Scientist-C?
faq.answer: The upper age limit shall not exceed 40 years, worked out on the closing date for applications. Government servants and employees of autonomous research organisations, research institutes and universities get a relaxation of up to five years. SC, ST, OBC and other categories get a relaxation as per Central Government orders.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary of ARI Pune Scientist-C?
faq.answer: Scientist-C is at Level-11 in the pay matrix, Rs.67700-208700, plus allowances as admissible.

faq.question: Q6. Are allowances paid on top of the Scientist-C pay?
faq.answer: Yes. Allowances are paid as admissible, and the benefits include NPS, Medical reimbursement, LTC etc., as presently admissible under the rules of the Institute.

faq.question: Q7. What is the application fee for ARI Pune Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The fee is Rs.500/-, non-refundable, paid online through SBI Collect. SC/ST and women candidates are excepted from the fee.

faq.question: Q8. How do I apply for ARI Pune Scientist-C?
faq.answer: Apply online at arijob.ourlib.in. Then send a printout with self-attested documents to the Director, Agharkar Research Institute, Gopal Ganesh Agarkar Road, Pune – 411 004, in an envelope superscribed "Application for <Post Code>".

faq.question: Q9. What is the selection process for ARI Pune Scientist-C?
faq.answer: Candidates may be shortlisted for interview, and shortlisted candidates are told by email the date, time and venue. A reserve panel from the interviewed candidates stays valid for one year.

faq.question: Q10. Is the ARI Pune Scientist-C post permanent?
faq.answer: Yes, both Scientist-C posts are permanent. They carry a one-year probation period that may be extended at the discretion of the Competent Authority.
